title: Rust: Match Expressions
description: Use Rust's powerful match expression for pattern matching.

steps.title: Match on Number
steps.description: Create a `number = 3` and match it: 1 -> "one", 2 -> "two", 3 -> "three", _ -> "other". Print the result.
hints: The `_` pattern catches all other values.
Match must be exhaustive — cover all possibilities.

verification.failureMessage: Print the English word for the number 3.

steps.title: Multiple Patterns
steps.description: Match a character `c = 'a'`: vowels (a, e, i, o, u) -> "vowel", other letters -> "consonant".
hints: The `|` operator means "or" within a match arm.

steps.title: Match with Ranges
hints: Ranges in match must be exhaustive and non-overlapping.

steps.title: Match as Expression
steps.description: Use match as an expression: match `day = 3` and assign the day name to a variable. Print the variable.
hints: Match expressions return a value that can be assigned.
Provide all 7 days and `_ => "invalid"` for the catch-all.

verification.failureMessage: Print the day name for day 3.

steps.title: Match with Guards
steps.description: Create a match on `number`: if number > 0 print "positive", if number < 0 print "negative". Use match guards with `if`.
hints: `match number { n if n > 0 => println!("positive"), n if n < 0 => println!("negative"), _ => println!("zero") }`
Guards add extra conditions to patterns.
Use `_` as a catch-all for zero.

verification.failureMessage: Print whether number is positive, negative, or zero.
